title: Marta
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Pesachim 103a we find: “Marta said in R' Yehoshua’s name: ניה״ק.” He is mentioned there alongside Levi and Mar, son of Ravna. It is not known who this Marta was or who this R' Yehoshua was. The better reading is that of Dikdukei Soferim there, note vav: “Marona, in the name of R' Yehoshua ben Levi.” The word Marona became corrupted into Marta when the vav and nun joined, producing a tav. He is in fact Marin, who spoke in R' Yehoshua ben Levi’s name in Eruvin 19a.[^1]

notes.text: The mnemonic ניה״ק is retained without an expansion; the earlier English “this is what he meant” was unsupported. Mar’s patronymic is printed רבנא and is transliterated Ravna without identifying him with another named sage. The customary work-name and personal-name expansions of דק״ס and רי״בל are Dikdukei Soferim and R' Yehoshua ben Levi; the specific edition has not been established here. The cited note is identified by the letter ו׳ (vav). The preference for Marona, the proposed joining of letters and the identification with Marin are Hyman’s textual argument, with its original confidence retained; they are not independently established identifications. Hyman’s Eruvin locator ends with two periods, יט..; 19a is its conventional reading, not a verified modern locus. Neither cited passage was independently checked.

The titles in ר׳ יהושע, דרי״בל and רי״בל are abbreviated. They are retained as R' in the English, including when the personal names are expanded. Neither a same-name identification nor Hyman’s preference for a variant reading supplies independent evidence for choosing a full title.
